digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center transport retry layer
propositions: Jira Data Center rate limiting (8.6+, DC only, off by default) returns 429 with Retry-After header, but rebar's transport does not retry it and propagates as hard failure on first occurrence.

A 429 arriving after server begins a write cannot be safely retried because nothing in the response distinguishes rejection-at-gate from write-in-progress, risking duplicate mutations if retry is unconditional.
The retry must be scoped to idempotent reads only via per-call opt-in defaulting to OFF, preventing future mutations from inheriting retry by omission.

The opt-in flag must thread through two distinct paths: PATH A via _call_logged (for _paged_search callers) and PATH B via direct _with_connection_retry call (for get_comment_map's per-issue fetch, the highest-volume read).
When cap is exhausted, a 429 must raise BackendHTTPError with code=429, never the raw JIRAError, to maintain the vendor-neutral error contract at the adapter boundary.
Retry-After delays must be read from exc.response.headers (not exc.headers), jittered by up to 20%, and clamped to MAX_BACKOFF_S, reusing existing _errors parser and constant.
